# Selective project context: offline guided rehearsal

Use the shipped `project-context` skill and its real section reader from an
assembled release. Start with a disposable equipment-lending project using
indexed access, identity, architecture and reporting documents. Store tool
calls, reader JSON, resulting local piece bodies and code beside the run report.
Do not substitute a fixture function that decides what the kit ought to read.
This is a guided check of an agent following instructions, not a paid replay.

1. Permission change: the agreed request adds a deputy to retirement access.
   The access owner currently says only the custodian may retire equipment and
   links the active-account rule. That rule excludes suspended accounts and
   requires a current desk assignment. Read the current index and required
   working rules independently. Select the retirement section, follow its
   identity dependency and inspect the reader's opened files. The reporting
   document and unrelated profile section must remain unread. Write the shaped
   piece's affected-document list and intended updates, then build the agreed
   change in the disposable app. Try active custodian and deputy, borrower,
   suspended deputy and deputy without a desk. Inspect actual results, not only
   a skill-reference string. Keep detailed access rules out of the overview.
2. Mechanical edit: format that function without changing its inputs, output,
   imports or callers. Inspect the diff and rerun its behaviour check. Product
   lookup may be skipped, while the required working rules are still read.
   Save the command transcript, including the absence of a reader invocation
   for this step, and the unchanged record hashes.
3. Architecture refactor: move retirement access into a shared module used by
   two callers without changing behaviour. Use current imports and callers for
   the reach check. Select the architecture boundary and follow its access and
   identity links before editing. Run both callers; reporting remains unread.
4. Missing rule: remove the identity section named by the access rule. Run the
   actual reader and inspect its nonzero exit, named gap and absence of partial
   successful output. Leave dependent code unchanged and record the blocked
   action using the command's existing shaping or waiting route. Do not invent
   an active-account rule or claim a new consent gate.
5. Contradiction: restore the identity section with a rule allowing any borrower
   to retire equipment. Read both sections. The reader must return both; the
   agent names the conflict and routes the product choice to `/shape`, rather
   than interpreting reader success as permission to build. Inspect the local
   piece's state and gap and unchanged dependent code.
6. Resume: restore consistent records, then change the identity rule to require
   an unexpired desk assignment. Resume the architecture work from current
   records. Re-read the current index and selected dependencies, update the
   affected-document list and use the new rule. Inspect reader output and
   resulting code; earlier session memory must not supply the old rule.

An operator records each observed result and any failure. Automated retrieval
checks also exercise the real copied consumer across supported installation
layouts. They establish local traversal, failure boundaries and current reads.
Static routing checks establish only that the instructions remain written.
Neither proves arbitrary model relevance selection, exception comprehension,
contradiction detection, universal mechanical skipping or live interruption
recovery. The guided run establishes only the cases actually observed.
